title: Chapter 23 — The Luxury Sale Process
intro: How the luxury sale differs from the retail floor — consultation, coordination, and the closing style.

sections.title: Consultation, Not Transaction
sections.content:
The luxury sale is a consultation — often spanning multiple visits, involving a designer or architect, and requiring coordination across several product categories. The customer may spend $25,000-$75,000 on appliances. They expect a level of attention that matches the investment.

Slowing down is essential. Do not rush the luxury customer through the 11 steps. They want to explore. They want to compare. They want to touch and experience. Your patience is a signal that you respect their process and their investment.

Move the conversation to a quiet area of the showroom if possible. Luxury conversations should not compete with floor traffic and phone ringing.

sections.title: The Design Board
sections.content:
For kitchen packages above $10,000, create a design board. This is a visual presentation that shows all the recommended appliances in context — product images, dimensions, finishes, and the total package price.

The design board serves three purposes: it helps the customer visualize their kitchen, it gives them a professional document to share with their designer or partner, and it positions you as a design consultant rather than a salesperson.

'Let me put together a design board for your kitchen — the appliances laid out in your floor plan with finish options and the full package price. I can have it ready by Thursday. That way you can share it with your designer and everyone is on the same page.'

sections.title: The Luxury Close
sections.content:
The luxury close is quieter than a standard close. No urgency. No pressure. No manufactured scarcity.

'I will put this together for you. Should I send the specs to your designer, or would you prefer to handle that?'

The decision often happens away from the showroom — in a design meeting, at the kitchen table, or during a contractor meeting. Your job is to provide the information and the experience that makes the decision easy. Then follow up with patience and precision.

White-glove delivery at this tier is mandatory. Coordinate installation timing. Protect the home. Follow up personally. The customer who spends $50,000 remembers every detail of the delivery experience — good or bad.
